This Banfield location used to be inside the PetSmart on Canal Street.  They were a good choice during those years.

I have had a certified service dog since 2014, and they were always capable of doing the travel paperwork necessary to take the dog overseas. At the PetSmart location I paid about $130 to get their vets signature on the documents.  The new location said “the system with the government is different” and they charged me over $700 for this submission to the USDA.  You’d expect at least the work would be foolproof and competent!  Sadly this new location screwed up the paperwork with the USDA on this occasion in August of 2026, and left me hanging with my required business trip to London.

I made the trip without the USDA paperwork solely because of the mistakes Banfield made in the submission.  The mistakes were so major that even while overseas the USDA would not issue the entry permit!  Fortunately because I had made this trip with my service dog several times previously, the Heathrow Airport Animal authorities had a record of my previous visits and were kind enough to have a local veterinarian review the dog’s health history and clear him for entry - at a cost exceeding $400 MORE.

This location has other issues that make it unsuitable for anyone’s pet.  The location has only street parking in front and the block is so dangerous with drug addicts and homeless it is scary dangerous.  The location requires that animals be left with them all day, in suspect conditions.   And Banfield pricing has gone through the roof! I am leaving this review regarding my experience with Dr. Laura Stowe.

First, I want to acknowledge that my dog, Seven, is overweight. I take full responsibility for that and have been actively working on his weight management. My issue is not with the medical information Dr. Stowe provided, but with how it was communicated.

During our phone conversation, I felt rushed and spoken to in a condescending manner. We discussed Seven’s weight, allergies, and treatment options. Dr. Stowe presented Cytopoint and Apoquel but did not explain the pros and cons of either option. As a first-time pet owner, I needed more information to make an informed decision rather than feeling pressured to choose on the spot.

When I picked Seven up after his dental procedure, I learned that no one had reviewed his bloodwork, thyroid screening, or my concerns about possible arthritis and joint issues. After I requested to speak with the veterinarian, Dr. Stowe came in and again focused heavily on Seven’s weight in a way that felt repetitive and dismissive. She also informed me that only a basic thyroid screening had been performed, but the different testing options had never been explained to me beforehand.

The most frustrating interaction occurred when I asked about Seven’s joints and possible arthritis. Instead of simply explaining her findings, she responded, “How do you think it’s doing?” As the veterinarian, I was asking because I genuinely did not know. A straightforward answer would have been more helpful and professional.

I did contact Banfield afterward to express my concerns. The manager listened and apologized, which I appreciated. However, I still felt it was important to leave this review because communication, bedside manner, and professionalism matter.

I understand that discussing a pet’s weight can be uncomfortable, and I agree that Seven’s weight is a concern. However, there is a respectful way to educate clients. Tone matters. The way questions are asked matters. The way information is delivered matters.

I have trusted Banfield with Seven’s care for the past three years and have invested significantly in his health. As a paying customer and first-time pet owner, I expect to be treated with respect and provided with clear explanations so I can make informed decisions for my pet.

I am not questioning Dr. Stowe’s medical knowledge. My concern is solely with her communication style and professionalism. Unfortunately, I left feeling talked down to rather than supported. For that reason, I will be requesting a different veterinarian for Seven moving forward.

When our dog was about one year old, he frequently scratched his eyes and head, often until the area bled. At that time, the veterinarian was unable to identify the cause but suspected heartworm and recommended multiple tests.

After conducting our own research, my husband discovered that our dog’s symptoms were consistent with allergies. Over the years, various veterinarians prescribed different allergy medications, but it was we who requested Cytopoint injections for him.

Recently, our dog began experiencing additional health issues. We brought him to Banfield twice within the past two weeks, but each time we received only general information and no clear diagnosis. Four days after the last visit, we had to take him to the emergency clinic. The veterinarians there determined that our dog had fluid accumulation in his abdomen, a heart murmur, possible heart failure, and several other complications.

It is deeply concerning that none of the veterinarians at Banfield identified his heart murmur or any of these underlying conditions. Our dog passed away peacefully at the emergency clinic last night. I got a new pup and was quoted about $380 for her vaccines. I have a thorough conversation with the tech about pricing, fees and whether or not to go with the wellness plan. The comparison was $380 without the wellness plan or $240 + $70 a month for the wellness plan (why would I ever do that right?? since everything isn’t covered and you have to pay anyway)  — I choose to not get the wellness plan and I leave my pup to get her vaccines. By the time I get home, I get a call from the front desk that the price I was quoted was wrong and that it would be over $600 for what I asked for (my dog had been out of my care for about 45 mins at this point). To bring the price down, I get half of the vaccines that I wanted and no heartworm medication because now I can’t afford it all. Already upset, I pick my pup up when she is ready and I’m told that was just her first round of vaccines (this was never discussed before) but now I’m locked in to go to Banfield since other vets have said it would be the best to continue her vaccines at the same place. – I called around. Again, already upset. I called Banfield and asked how much my pups vaccines will be in totality for the next round and I’m told $130 — I put it on my calendar so I know it was correct. I agreed to the $130 and I schedule the next appointment. On the day of the appointment )today) I call just before I leave my house and I’m told it would be $110 to my surprise. When I arrive and I’m talking to the tech, I’m told it would actually be $155 for two vaccines since the office visit itself is $80.

Look, I don’t know what’s going on with Banfield but every time I leave, I’m paying more than what I came in there for and I will not be coming back

5/30 Update: After Banfield’s initial comment, I followed up via email to share my concerns in more detail. Today, I received a call from Banfield South Loop.

The call began with a pitch for their $70/month wellness plan—even though my dog is fully vaccinated for the year, which they know as her vet. I explained I didn’t sign up because the initial quoted costs were actually higher with the plan. As we now know, the original pricing was incorrect due to a tech’s mistake, so I never got to make a fully informed decision. I never got the opportunity to calculate costs or even choose a different vet after getting my estimate because at the time that Banfield called me with the mistake on their part my dog was already out of my care for 45 mins and already administered care.

My main concern is the lack of price transparency—unclear communication about vaccine series, inconsistent pricing, and vague explanations. I was told the tech was “new,” but that doesn’t change the fact that I’ve now spent hundreds more because of their error.

When I asked why my $80 visit cost more than just the two $45 vaccines, I was told an exam is required before vaccinations. That’s fine—but the vet never touched my dog during our time in the exam room. I did not leave my dog at Banfield this time and was in and out in 20 mins and was only separated from my dog for five minutes while they took her to the back for the vaccines. I was told the exam happened then, without my knowledge or consent. That should have been disclosed upfront.

To be clear, I don’t believe the medical care has been poor, —but the administrative confusion, upselling, and lack of transparency have made this a 0-star experience.

I should have read all these bad reviews and seen their low rating before taking my sick puppy to this clinic. I took her in for vomiting and diarrhea; I think she was already dehydrated. These people did nothing to hydrate her. They kept her there all day without giving her anything, even though her tests showed she had a parasite (they ruled out parvovirus). I picked her up in the afternoon, and I noticed she was very sedated, which I don't understand. Why did they have to sedate or put her to sleep if she was just a miniature puppy of only 3 months old? She wasn't aggressive or restless; she was just sick. These people apparently didn't give her any medication, nor did they hydrate her. When we took her home, they explained the parasite she had and how we should give her the medication, which we did exactly as instructed. She was fast asleep, and we thought it was normal. Around 9 pm, our baby tried to get up but started wandering around the house, confused, and stumbling from side to side. We continued to think this was normal and that she would be fine the next day when the effects of the "sedative" they had given her (without our consent) wore off. Bedtime arrived, and we did our best to protect her bed so she wouldn't hit the wall in her confusion.
We went to sleep, and at 5 am, we woke up to give her her medicine, but our puppy was dead. We don't understand what happened, what they gave her, or in what quantities, because this isn't even written in her medical record.
If she looked so sick, why didn't they do anything? We have so many questions; we don't understand anything about what happened.
